guitar.modelsText: Fender Jazzmaster / Gibson Les Paul / Gretsch
guitar.notes: Turner has used Jazzmasters, Gibson ES-335/Les Pauls, and various others over the band's career; no single iconic instrument, so medium confidence is appropriate.

tone.target: jangly edge-of-breakup indie rock with bright mids and slight grit
tone.profile: jangly edge-of-breakup indie rock with bright mids and slight grit
tone.summary: A clean signal path utilizing a mild boost and OD pedal to achieve the 'jangly edge-of-breakup' sound, paired with an AC30-style amp simulation and bright cab, finished with subtle reverb.
corrections: keep it more jangly than crunchy

rig.name: Arctic Monkeys - When The Sun Goes Down - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly push the signal for controlled breakup and brightness.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of a dedicated OD to maintain clarity while adding grit.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary 'jangly edge-of-breakup' grit without sounding overly distorted.
blocks.gap: Red Haze is chosen for its bright, mid-focused breakup character, mimicking classic Vox/AC30 tones.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, mid-forward sound of a Vox AC30 combo.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the AC30 simulation.
blocks.gap: While not strictly required by the tone, this cab choice reinforces the desired UK/British rock aesthetic.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the bright mids and cut any excessive low-end rumble.
Optional subtle modulation for added depth (kept off by default per corrections).
blocks.gap: The instructions explicitly advise dropping chorus, so this module is included but deactivated.

blocks.purpose: Add light room ambience to give the sound space without sounding muddy.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the jangly, bright British tone required for Arctic Monkeys.

proposals.reason: The current UK Vintage cab is too generic; a specific AC30 IR will enhance the desired jangly, bright British tone.
